blockers.title: Three paths change outside the declared closed roster while basedOn.method asserts nothing outside it changed
detail: basedOn.method declares a thirteen-entry closed roster — /artifact, /version, /date, /basedOn, /appliesFindingsOf, /honestyRepairsFromV1, /mandatoryStorageRule/d002FirstSlice, /sliceStanding, /identityDependencies, /storageMandateTextCarriedVerbatim, /reviewGuidance, /reMeasurementAtV1, /reMeasurementAtV2 — and closes with 'Every path neither the roster nor succession metadata names is unchanged from v1.'
I flattened both generations to leaf JSON paths and diffed: 13 changed, 37 added, 2 removed. Three of those fall outside the roster.

/authorityClaim CHANGED and is the clearest instance. v1 read 'This artifact PROPOSES the DR-106 leftover T2-02 extraction: the signed authoritative offline analysis closure contents…'; v2 reads 'This artifact PROPOSES the DR-106 leftover T2-02 extraction for the later slice that includes authoritative offline closure. D-002 records that slice 1 is local/non-authoritative only and that DR-106 is deferred WHOLLY — a recorded disposition, not silence.' That is a substantive rewrite of the artifact's headline authority statement. /authorityClaim appears on no roster entry, and honestyRepairsFromV1 names only d002FirstSlice and sliceStanding as the locations of that repair, so no succession metadata names it either.

/recordedInputs/governingSources/3/sha256 CHANGED from 0833973f… to 7da75955…, and /recordedInputs/governingSources/3/role CHANGED to a new HEAD and a new set of named properties. /recordedInputs appears on no roster entry.

This is not a cosmetic accounting point. The rewritten authorityClaim is one of the two operative locations both frozen v1 blockers named — Codex's OACV1-B1 location list opens with /recordedInputs/governingSources/3/role and includes /authorityClaim — so the successor edited the exact text the blockers were about, correctly, and then omitted both paths from the roster that is supposed to make such edits auditable.
blockers.fairnessNote: The two /recordedInputs legs are the weaker half of this finding. honestyRepairsFromV1 does say 'ADV-OACC-V1-01: remasurement is at HEAD 7acef4f / COORD 7da75955, standing LIVE', which names the new digest even though it describes the remeasurement block rather than recordedInputs, so a generous reading of 'succession metadata names' could cover the sha256. No such reading is available for /authorityClaim: nothing in the roster or the succession metadata mentions it at all, and it changed. The blocker stands on that leg alone.
blockers.whyBlockerGrade: Roster completeness is the mechanism that makes a successor auditable, and the completeness sentence is an affirmative claim the artifact makes about itself. A successor that states 'every path neither the roster nor succession metadata names is unchanged' while three paths outside it changed has made a false statement about its own diff — and it did so on the very edit its predecessor was rejected for. The content of all three changes is correct and I am not asking for any of it to be reverted.
blockers.minimumRepair: Add /authorityClaim and /recordedInputs/governingSources to the closed roster in basedOn.method. No byte of the changed content needs to move. If the intent was that the remeasurement standing rule already covers the governing-source repin, say so explicitly in the method rather than leaving it to inference.
